title: Packaging and packaging waste consultation: EU national registers of producers
summary: Opportunity to comment on proposed rules on registers of packaging producers in EU countries for Extended Producer …
update:
New European Union (EU) rules on packaging and packaging waste (PPWR, Regulation 2025/40 ) require each EU Member State to establish a national register of packaging producers to monitor compliance with Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) requirements. EPR aims to ensure that producers of products are financially and/or organisationally responsible for managing the waste stage of a product’s life cycle.

The European Commission is now proposing rules on how Member States should establish these registers of packaging producers in their country.

Each individual Member State may also choose to include in their register non-EU producers of packaged products (including food), who will need to appoint an authorised representative for EPR to carry out these obligations on their behalf.

This proposal sets standardised formats for registration of packaging producers and for reporting, and specifies the information that must be submitted. This will ensure consistency across all EU countries.
what_changing: The PPWR (Regulation 2025/40 ) introduces the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) scheme, under which packaging producers are financially responsible for managing the waste stage of the packaging’s life cycle, for example by organising or paying for the collection and disposal of waste.
why:
By setting standardised formats for registration and reporting, the European Commission aims to reduce the administrative burden and avoid divergent national registration systems.

The PPWR sets new rules for packaging and packaged products put on the EU market, including the management of packaging waste. It has introduced the EPR scheme for packaging to make all packaging reusable or recyclable by 2030, and to reduce (over) packaging and packaging waste.

See New EU packaging rules explained .
timeline: The Regulation is expected to be published in the fourth quarter of 2026, and will enter into force 20 days after publication. From that date, EU Member States will have 18 months to establish a national register of producers.
actions:
All interested stakeholders are invited to give feedback via the European Commission’s Have Your Say platform until 10 September 2026 .

Stakeholders wishing to respond must be registered. Those who do not already have an account will first need to Create an EU login account , then register their organisation on the EU Transparency register .
background:
Packaging is one of the main users of virgin materials and is a significant contributor to waste. While the share of recycled packaging has been growing slowly in the EU between 2014 and 2023 ( European Commission 2025 ), much recyclable packaging is still not recycled. This is because there are not enough suitable, economically viable collection and recycling processes.

The PPWR is part of the EU’s circular economy action plan ( European Commission 2020 ) which commits to making all packaging reusable or recyclable by 2030, and to reducing (over) packaging and packaging waste.
